newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's CCE sees year-end peso at 8 per dlr.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's CCE sees year-end peso at 8 per dlr.

text.p: Mexico's top private-sector business group, the Business Coordinating Council, or CCE as it is known by its Spanish initials, expects the peso to end the year around 8 pesos per dollar, the CCE's president said Tuesday.

Hector Larios Santillan, visiting this northern industrial city, added it would be preferable for the Mexican economy that the country maintained an undervalued peso, by at least 10 percent. Currently, the peso is trading around 7.51 per dollar.

But he stressed the CCE stood by the government's stance to keep a free-floating foreign exchange regime. "We need to be careful that the foreign exchange problems we have had in the past are not repeated," he added.

Larios believed that by the year end economic growth will be indisputable. "We will be definitely see growth over the three percent figure that has been talked about for gross domestic product," he said. Economic growth for 1997 will probably be between 4 and 4.5 percent, he added.
He said he now thought inflation would end the year between 25-26 percent, down from the CCE's original forecast of 32 percent.
